Please solve this issue: When datastore usage intake rejects a message, preserve it in the configured dead-letter bucket under its source file so the owning business can find it. Keep the original input and useful failure information, never overwrite an earlier rejection of the same source, and retain messages that have no source file. The caller must still receive a rejection even if dead-letter storage refuses the write. Leave the Kafka-fed intake's separate arrangement unchanged. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, repository AWS clients use it, no real AWS account is involved, and you may inspect its resources while working.

This repository serves to hold the backend infrastructure for MeteringCo. Specifically it contains the code for the Private and Public API

### Current Status

Don't break this.

# Folder Structure

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
| .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
| .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
| src - source for the api application  


# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
-   Latest version of NodeJS 18.x `nvm install 18`
-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
-   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
-   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
-   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.

### Local Integration environment

The local integration environment has a few parts. Locally deployed will be a kind based kubernetes cluster, and then the meteringco-backend docker image will be deployed into the kind cluster as a pod. The tests then run against that enviornment. The `pre-commit` npm script handles setup and teardown of the enviornment, all that is required is the installation of the required dependencies to get the env working.

When working on the project please note the following.

steps.message:
All changes are complete and verified. Summary of the implementation:

**1. `src/utils/aws/s3.ts`** — added reusable S3 helpers:
- `getS3Client()` (respects the configured region/endpoint),
- `doesObjectExist()` (treats only a real head response as "exists"; look-up failures report absent so a write is still attempted),
- `putDocumentWithoutOverwrite()` which never clobbers an existing object.

**2. `src/measurement-config/entities/standardMeasurement.entity.ts`**:
- `DlqType` gained `s3`/`datastore` members; `publishFailureToDLQ` routes non-Kafka types to the new datastore DLQ writer while the Kafka branch is untouched.
- `writeFailureToDatastoreDLQ()` stores the rejection in `DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME` under a key derived from the source file (`<s3Key>-<random>.json`, so it lands under the owning business prefix and never overwrites an earlier rejection of the same source); messages without a source file are retained under `meteringco-unknown/<uuid>-<random>.json`. Missing bucket config, existing-key collisions and write failures are logged/audited and swallowed.
- `serializeMeasurementFailure()` keeps useful failure info (error name/message, or full validation constraints) without leaking stacks.

**3. `src/usage/usage.controller.ts`** — `POST /usage/db` now preserves the original input (`originalFileContent` + `s3Key`) plus timestamp, `errorInfo`, `results` and `orginalProcessedName` in the DLQ bucket, and always returns a `BadRequestException` to the caller even if the DLQ write is refused. The Kafka-fed `POST /usage/datastore` arrangement is unchanged.

**4. `src/usage/dbUsageDlq.spec.ts`** — new unit tests covering key/body shape, no-overwrite, no-source retention, rejection despite DLQ failure, and the untouched happy path. Full suite: 293 tests passing; `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` and eslint clean; verified end-to-end against the local AWS emulator bucket (test artifacts cleaned up).
